It sounds like you're feeling a lot of pressure from your advisor, and that can be really overwhelming. It's completely understandable that you might feel like you're walking on eggshells around her.

Since you mentioned she tends to make things "miserable," I want to gently suggest that maybe the way she communicates isn't necessarily about you being bad or failing, but rather about her own high standards or stress. Sometimes, people who are tough on the outside are actually trying to protect themselves or others from disappointment.

Would you be willing to try setting those micro deadlines I mentioned earlier, even if it feels scary to reach out to her? Sometimes having a clear plan and small wins can help shift the dynamic, and it might give you a bit more confidence to talk to her about how you're feeling.

evidence.quote: My advisor is a tough woman, I'm not going to beat around the bush. She tends to make everything miserable.
Yes, but I've been really bad about keeping her in the loop. I feel bad when I fall behind, and then I'm fearful of getting back in touch with her.

It has always helped me. For example, you can break it down into 4 weeks, then each week write your goals -- maybe put call Advisor or go stop by every week, but I would put that first for the first week.

That is why a time line is good. For example, you make a goal that you will work on your reference and citation page for one hour, after that, you are DONE, If you have time at the end, you can revisit it. The hour is my suggestion, you make your own. lol THAT way, you don't get caught going on and on for 6 hours to make it perfect. One hour is reasonable.
That definitely sounds reasonable. Putting micro deadlines in might be what I need to do to keep me focused.
